story: The creator god Pacha Kamaq was worshipped by the people of Peru before the Inca conquest. When the Inca conquered them, they added him to their own pantheon, though they considered him less powerful than their supreme god Viracocha. The myths about him are contradictory. Some accounts claim he was the cowardly brother of Manco Cápac, called Ayca. Other accounts say that he, Manco Cápac, and Viracocha were the three sons of Inti, the sun god. Another myth relates that Pacha Kamaq made the first man and the first woman but forgot to give them food, so the man died. The woman then prayed over Pacha Kamaq's head to Inti, his father, asking to be made the mother of all the peoples of the earth. Pacha Kamaq became furious, and as her children were born one by one, he tried to kill them. He was ultimately beaten and thrown into the sea by her hero-son, Wichama. After this defeat, Pacha Kamaq gave up his violent struggle and instead became content to rule as the supreme god of fish.
